title: Wren and the Sigil
premise: Emrys Zhou, exiled for a storm she swears she never called, keeps ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things — a smugglers' exchange dealing in bottled memories, unmade vows, and other contraband of fate. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies, she is seized by the prophecy's own logic and delivered to the frozen capital, where a beloved king is slowly being replaced by the sigil-crown that wears him. Guided by a disgraced royal oathbreaker named Sable and the guild's treacherous master, Emrys discovers the storm that ruined her was the crown's first attempt to summon her — she is the unbinding the prophecy demands, and its final sacrifice. In the long winter's last night, Emrys tears the sigil from the king at the cost of her own storm-gift, chooses truth over the guild's lies, and earns not a throne or pardon but a home: the guild remade, the king human again, and Sable staying by choice rather than oath.
about_author: Casper Zhou is the pen name of a former shipping clerk who spent nine years cataloguing oddities in a warehouse and now catalogs them in novels instead. They write cold, luminous fantasy about people who keep records of things that should not exist.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Emrys, guild clerk in the port city of Vell, audits a shipment of bottled thunderstorms and records a debt she knows can never be collected. Her POV establishes her exile, her precision, and her loneliness. Beat: competent isolation, a life built to avoid being needed.

chapters.title: A Date in Old Ink
chapters.summary: Cataloguing a seized estate's library, Emrys finds the Codex Vellum, a prophecy book, and reads tonight's date written a century ago — followed by her own true name. Her POV; wonder curdling to dread. Beat: the past reaching for her.

chapters.title: The Guild's Quiet Price
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane reveals he has known about the Codex for years and has been selling 'passage to the chosen one' to royal agents. Emrys's POV; betrayal. Beat: the one institution that took her in has been selling her.

chapters.title: Riders on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Royal oathbreakers arrive to collect Emrys; she flees through the guild's impossible warehouse, where doors open onto wrong seasons. Sable, a disgraced knight, catches her — and lets her go. Sable's POV. Beat: an enemy who hesitates.

chapters.title: Taken by the Prophecy
chapters.summary: The Codex activates; the words pull Emrys across the country in a night of collapsing distances, depositing her in the frozen capital of Carreth. Her POV, disoriented and furious. Beat: agency stolen — the prophecy moves her like a piece.

chapters.title: The King Who Smiles Wrong
chapters.summary: Court presentation: King Aldous is beloved, warm, perfect — and Emrys sees the sigil-crown drinking him, his pauses lengthening, his eyes lagging. Her POV. Beat: horror behind charm.

chapters.title: A Cell with Good Light
chapters.summary: Imprisoned as a 'guest of prophecy,' Emrys maps the palace from her tower room and discovers the previous storm-callers' cells scratched with warnings. Her POV. Beat: she is the latest in a line of summoned sacrifices.

chapters.title: Sable's Oathbreaker Winter
chapters.summary: Sable, assigned to guard her, recounts how she broke her oath to protect the old queen from the crown's first hunger — and was exiled for the truth. Sable's POV. Beat: two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Storm Remembered
chapters.summary: Emrys confesses the storm that caused her exile; Sable realizes the crown summoned it hunting for her years early. Her POV, grief reframed. Beat: her worst night was never her fault.

chapters.title: The Queen Dowager's Garden
chapters.summary: The dowager queen, half-forgotten, tells Emrys how the sigil was bound to the royal line — a bargain made to end an older war. Her POV. Beat: the villain was once a rescue.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives
chapters.summary: Corvane reaches the capital as the crown's licensed supplier of impossible things; he offers Emrys freedom in exchange for legitimizing the guild's prophecy trade. His POV. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Lies
chapters.summary: Emrys finds Corvane's true ledger: the guild has fed the crown a dozen 'chosen ones' before her, all dead. Her POV; cold rage. Beat: loyalty to the guild dies on the page.

chapters.title: First Frost of the Long Winter
chapters.summary: The winter stops behaving — snow falls upward, rivers freeze mid-current — as the sigil accelerates its feeding. Sable's POV. Beat: the stakes turn existential.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite, Half-Read
chapters.summary: Emrys deciphers the Codex's unbinding: the sigil can be torn free only by a storm-caller who gives up the storm. Her POV. Beat: hope with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: A Night of Borrowed Honesty
chapters.summary: Trapped by a curfew blizzard, Emrys and Sable trade the truths they've withheld — Sable's love for the old queen, Emrys's fear that she's nothing without her gift. Alternating POV. Beat: love begins as honesty.

chapters.title: The King, Briefly Himself
chapters.summary: Aldous surfaces for one lucid hour, begs Emrys to unbind him, and describes the crown's interior: a century of kings, still in there, screaming politely. His POV. Beat: the victim given a voice.

chapters.title: Corvane's Counterfeit Codex
chapters.summary: Corvane plants a forged prophecy naming Sable as the sacrifice, hoping Emrys will trade her friend for herself. His POV. Beat: the trap of self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Snow Court
chapters.summary: Emrys publicly denounces the forged Codex before the court, exposing Corvane's forgery and her own guild's trade — burning her last bridge home. Her POV. Beat: truth chosen over belonging.

chapters.title: Prisoner of Both Sides
chapters.summary: The crown, threatened, has Sable arrested; Emrys is confined to the Codex chamber, where the book begins writing her next days before she lives them. Her POV. Beat: the walls close on every side.

chapters.title: Sable in the Deep Cells
chapters.summary: Sable endures interrogation by the crown's Regent — actually the sigil's chief servant — and refuses to name Emrys as the willing sacrifice. Sable's POV. Beat: loyalty under torture.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns Its Coat
chapters.summary: Corvane's own clerks, led by Emrys's old apprentice Tamsin, smuggle her the real ledger and the warehouse keys. Tamsin's POV. Beat: the family Emrys thought lost chooses her back.

chapters.title: Through the Impossible Doors
chapters.summary: Emrys and Tamsin open the warehouse doors onto the palace undercroft, walking through wrong seasons to reach the cells. Emrys's POV. Beat: the guild's magic turned to rescue.

chapters.title: The Regent Unmasked
chapters.summary: Confrontation in the deep cells: the Regent is the first king the sigil ever wore, a hollow man animated by the crown's will. Emrys's POV; revulsion and pity. Beat: the villain is the prophecy's first victim.

chapters.title: What Sable Would Not Say
chapters.summary: Freed, Sable refuses to flee the city, insisting on standing at the unbinding — not from duty now, but from love. Sable's POV. Beat: duty transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: The Dowager's Confession
chapters.summary: The dowager queen reveals she bound the sigil originally to save her dying husband — and has been paying its price in memories ever since. Her POV. Beat: guilt as the engine of the whole tragedy.

chapters.title: The Codex Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: The prophecy book, sensing the unbinding near, begins offering Emrys versions where everyone lives — if she only agrees to wear the crown instead. Her POV. Beat: the most seductive lie.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Ledger Entry
chapters.summary: Corvane, ruined by exposure, attempts to sell the sigil the unbinding rite itself; Tamsin and the clerks intercept him in the warehouse. Tamsin's POV. Beat: the merchant undone by his own accounting.

chapters.title: Assembly of the Unwilling
chapters.summary: Emrys gathers her improbable alliance — oathbreaker, dowager, clerks, one lucid king — and each must consent to a plan that may kill them. Her POV. Beat: belonging built from the broken.

chapters.title: The Longest Night Begins
chapters.summary: Winter solstice: the sigil's feeding peaks, the sun fails to rise, and the unbinding must happen before dawn or the crown completes its century. Alternating POV. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Storm Over Carreth
chapters.summary: Emrys calls the storm she was exiled for — deliberately this time — and rides it through the palace's frozen halls. Her POV. Beat: her curse becomes her weapon.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: The sigil speaks through every king it has worn, offering Emrys her exile undone, her guild restored, her storm kept — for one small signature. Her POV. Beat: the final temptation.

chapters.title: Sable's Stand at the Door
chapters.summary: Sable holds the throne room door alone against the Regent and the crown's guards, buying Emrys minutes with her broken oath reforged. Sable's POV. Beat: loyalty proven in blood and choice.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: On the dais, Emrys tears the sigil from Aldous's head, pouring her storm-gift into the rite as the Codex demands. Her POV; agony and release. Beat: the climax — the price paid.

chapters.title: What the Crown Let Go
chapters.summary: A century of kings pours out of the dying sigil — brief, grateful ghosts — before it crumbles, and the sun claws above the horizon. Aldous's POV. Beat: grief and dawn together.

chapters.title: The Cost, Tallied
chapters.summary: Emrys wakes powerless and half-frozen; the storm is gone and may never return. Sable stays anyway, with no oath left to justify it. Alternating POV. Beat: love without duty's excuse.

chapters.title: A King Made Human
chapters.summary: Aldous, mortal and diminished, chooses to abdicate rather than rule on borrowed warmth, and asks Emrys to keep the true ledger of his reign. His POV. Beat: humility as restoration.

chapters.title: The Guild of Possible Things
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Emrys recharter the guild, trading only in things that can be honestly owned — and Emrys is offered, and takes, a place in it. Tamsin's POV. Beat: belonging, finally earned.

chapters.title: Pardon, With Conditions
chapters.summary: The new regency pardons Emrys for a storm she never called; she signs the pardon and files it, then files her own account of what really happened. Her POV. Beat: the record set straight at last.

chapters.title: The Codex Goes Blank
chapters.summary: The prophecy book, its purpose served, empties page by page — except one line naming no one, promising only a long spring. Emrys's POV. Beat: the future reopened.

chapters.title: Wren and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Spring in Vell: Emrys, called 'Wren' again by the clerks who stayed, teaches Sable the ledgers and feels, for once, unremarkable and home. Her POV closes the book. Beat: quiet joy after the impossible.
